description: Research and prototype RLM (Recursive Language Model) integration from Alex Zhang paper

userStories.title: Analyze rlms library architecture
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to understand how the rlms library works internally so I can evaluate integration options.
acceptanceCriteria: Clone https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm and read source code
Document how rlm.completion() orchestrates decomposition
Document REPL environment interface (methods, state management)
Document how recursive calls are tracked and results aggregated
Document prompt templates used for decomposition and synthesis
Document sandbox backend abstraction (local, Docker, Modal)
Save analysis to docs/rlm-analysis.md in the repo
userStories.notes: Analysis saved to docs/rlm-analysis.md covering all acceptance criteria

userStories.title: Map RLM concepts to Orchestra infrastructure
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to identify which Orchestra components correspond to RLM concepts and where gaps exist.
acceptanceCriteria: Create mapping table: RLM concept → Orchestra equivalent → Gap
Identify SubAgent ↔ sub-LM calls, Daytona ↔ REPL, stream_generator ↔ rlm.completion
Document gaps that need bridging for each integration option
Add mapping to docs/rlm-analysis.md
userStories.notes: Mapping table with 13 concepts, detailed gap analysis for 5 critical/significant gaps, and component-level diagram added to docs/rlm-analysis.md section 9

userStories.title: Evaluate integration options
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a clear comparison of all integration approaches so the team can choose the best path.
acceptanceCriteria: Evaluate Option A: Direct rlms library integration with pros/cons/effort
Evaluate Option B: LangGraph native implementation with pros/cons/effort
Evaluate Option C: Hybrid rlms + LangGraph streaming with pros/cons/effort
Evaluate Option D: Tool-based exposure with pros/cons/effort
Include streaming/UI visibility analysis for each option
Save comparison to docs/rlm-recommendation.md
userStories.notes: Comprehensive evaluation of 4 options (Direct rlms, Native LangGraph, Hybrid, Tool-Based) with pros/cons/effort, comparison matrix, streaming/UI visibility deep dive, risk assessment, and migration path analysis saved to docs/rlm-recommendation.md

userStories.title: Build proof of concept
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a working prototype to validate the recommended approach.
acceptanceCriteria: Install rlms in backend venv or create isolated test script
Create backend/scripts/rlm_prototype.py that runs rlm.completion()
Test with a large input such as analyzing the Orchestra codebase
Measure and document latency, cost, quality vs standard completion
Document findings in docs/rlm-recommendation.md
userStories.notes: Prototype at backend/scripts/rlm_prototype.py. Benchmark: standard 30.4s/$0.007 vs RLM 76.5s/$0.054 (2.5x slower, 7.4x costlier for within-context inputs). Confirmed streaming gap and FINAL_VAR extraction bug. Results in docs/rlm-benchmark-results.md, findings added to docs/rlm-recommendation.md Section 11.

userStories.title: Design full integration architecture
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an architecture design for the production integration.
acceptanceCriteria: Document where RLM fits in agent construction pipeline
Document how recursive steps stream to frontend
Document how UI shows decomposition progress
Document how sandbox environments are configured
Document how cost tracking works across recursive calls
Include dependency on #694 subagent UI for rendering recursive steps
Add architecture to docs/rlm-recommendation.md
userStories.notes: Full architecture for Option D (Tool-Based) added as Section 12 of docs/rlm-recommendation.md. Covers: agent pipeline integration (12.1), 3 tool specifications (12.2), streaming design (12.3), UI rendering (12.4), sandbox configuration (12.5), cost tracking (12.6), end-to-end data flow (12.7), skill migration path (12.8), dependencies including #694 (12.9), and phased implementation plan (12.10).
